name: Scientific Calculator
title: Scientific Calculator
language: English by default; Romanian is available in Settings
short: Scientific calculations, RPN, number bases, constants and unit conversions.
description:
Work through scientific calculations with algebraic entry or an optional RPN stack. Switch between decimal, hexadecimal, octal and binary modes. Use trigonometric and logarithmic functions, constants, unit conversions and a local calculation history.

The app opens in English. Romanian is available in Settings. Calculations work offline and no account is needed. History stores up to 50 results on your device.

Real-number calculations use finite precision. Check important results independently. Developed by Traian Anghel and published by Praxis Science Lab.
data: Calculation history (up to 50 results), number formatting, angle and base preferences, and language are stored in app-private storage. Calculations run on the device. The app does not transmit these records to Praxis Science Lab. No accounts, advertising, analytics or crash-reporting service are implemented.
permissions: No camera, microphone, contacts or location permission is requested. The Android package declares Internet access through its framework, but the calculator has no application network requests and over-the-air updates are disabled. Opening the privacy or publisher link uses your browser.
retention: Clear calculation history in the app to remove saved results. Clear the app's storage in Android Settings or uninstall to remove its remaining local settings and records. Android cloud backup is disabled for this app. Praxis Science Lab has no server copy to restore.
safety: A calculation tool for learning and general use. Results have finite numerical precision; verify important calculations independently.
checks: Launch, calculate 2 + 3 = 5 and recover from an invalid operation with AC.
Switch ALG/RPN, angle units and DEC/HEX/OCT/BIN; verify expected sample results.
Open constants and conversions; save and clear calculation history.
Change language, restart, use airplane mode and open Privacy policy from About.
gaps: Final upload-key-signed AAB and verification on a physical Android device are still required.
Complete account verification, actual audience/IARC forms, and the closed test required by the account.

name: Atomic Clock
title: Atomic Clock
short: Check network time, compare time zones and use a stopwatch or countdown.
description:
Compare your device clock with network time. Atomic Clock queries time servers using NTP and can use an HTTPS fallback when configured. View synchronization status and the measured clock offset, choose time zones, and use a stopwatch or countdown.

Select a time server, adjust synchronization settings and choose a 12-hour or 24-hour display. English, Romanian and Spanish are available.

Synchronization needs an Internet connection. Displayed accuracy depends on the server, network and device. This is a general time utility, not a certified time reference. Published by Praxis Science Lab.
data: Server choice, synchronization settings, the last synchronization result and selected time zones are stored on your device. To synchronize, the app sends network time requests to the selected server and configured fallbacks. Recipients see your source IP address, request timing and protocol information. The HTTPS fallback also sends an app-identifying User-Agent. The app does not create an account or send a location-sensor reading, and has no advertising or analytics SDK.
permissions: Internet access is used for NTP and optional HTTPS synchronization. The default server is time.cloudflare.com. Fallbacks include NTP Pool hosts; Google Time, Apple Time and a custom host can also be selected. If a server fails, other configured providers may be contacted. NTP uses UDP and is not encrypted. The Cloudflare HTTPS fallback uses encrypted transport. Server operators process connection information under their own policies; a custom server is controlled by its operator.
retention: Remove saved time-zone entries in the app. Clear app storage in Android Settings or uninstall to remove local app records. This build does not explicitly disable Android backup, so device backup or transfer settings may retain or restore app preferences. Remove any device backup separately if needed. Remote server logs are controlled by the time-service operators; clearing app storage does not delete those logs.
safety: Network time accuracy varies. Do not rely on the app as a certified or safety-critical timing instrument.
checks: Synchronize on Wi-Fi and mobile data; inspect the server, offset and status.
Disable connectivity and verify the offline/last-sync information.
Add and remove a time zone, test stopwatch and countdown, restart and check settings.
Open privacy information and test a failed custom server and the fallback behavior.
gaps: Data safety needs provider-level review of IP/request processing and retention. Do not submit an unqualified no-data-collected answer.
NTP traffic is unencrypted: do not declare all transmitted data encrypted.
Recheck the prepared screenshots against the final signed AAB and verify native libraries and physical-device behavior.

name: Frequency Sound Generator
title: Frequency Sound Generator
short: Generate tones, explore waveforms, run frequency sweeps and export WAV files.
description:
Explore sound with sine, square, sawtooth and triangle waves. Set a frequency, choose the output channel, adjust volume and run a frequency sweep. Save presets, select musical notes, set a stop timer and export a generated WAV file.

Generation and settings work on your device without an account. English, Romanian and Spanish are available. Actual audible output depends on your device, speakers and headphones.

Start at a low volume and keep listening sessions comfortable. This app is not a hearing test, medical treatment or calibrated measurement instrument. Published by Praxis Science Lab.
data: Generator settings, language, presets and the last generator state are stored locally. Audio is synthesized on your device. Exported WAV files are written to a destination managed by the device. The app has no account, advertising SDK, analytics service or application backend and does not upload presets or generated audio to Praxis Science Lab.
permissions: The Android release does not request microphone access. A legacy write-storage permission is limited to Android API 28 and below for WAV export. Newer Android versions use the platform's file/media facilities. If you open or share an exported file with another service, that destination handles the file under its own policy.
retention: Delete saved presets using the app's controls. Clear Android app storage or uninstall to remove private settings. Exported WAV files remain in your selected destination until you delete them separately. Android backup is not explicitly disabled in this build; device backup and transfer settings can retain preferences. Copies you share with another service must be managed there.
safety: Start at low volume. Frequency settings do not guarantee speaker output or calibrated sound levels. No hearing-test or therapeutic claims are made.
checks: At a low device volume, start and stop each waveform; verify silence after Stop.
Test left/right output, a short sweep and timer auto-stop.
Save and delete a preset, export a short WAV and open it from the selected destination.
Background the app during output, restart, and check language and privacy links.
gaps: Recheck screenshots against the final signed AAB and inspect merged permissions, legacy export and physical-device audio behavior.

name: AudioLab
title: AudioLab
short: Explore audio locally with spectrum tools, signal generation and file analysis.
description:
Explore audio signals on your Android device. Use live microphone analysis, waveform and spectrum views, a spectrogram, signal generation and local audio-file analysis. Save sessions and export available charts or reports.

Microphone access is requested when you start live analysis. Files are selected through the system picker. Processing and session storage are local, with no app account or cloud upload. English, Romanian and Spanish are available.

Displayed levels and analysis depend on the device, microphone and signal. AudioLab is not a calibrated sound-level meter or a medical or hearing-diagnostic tool. Start generated audio at low volume. Published by Praxis Science Lab.
data: Live microphone samples and user-selected audio files are processed on your device. AudioLab stores preferences, session names and state, file references and numeric measurement records in its private local database. Microphone analysis is started by the user and stops when the app leaves the foreground. The app has no account, analytics, advertising or cloud service. The Android release removes Internet and network-state permissions.
permissions: RECORD_AUDIO is requested for live analysis. You can deny or revoke it in Android Settings and continue with features that do not need the microphone. Audio-file access is granted through the system picker. Exporting a chart, session or PDF writes the information you choose to a system-selected destination, which may be a cloud-backed document provider. Such a provider handles its copy under its own policy. The app does not automatically upload microphone audio.
retention: Saved sessions can be deleted in the app. Clear Android app storage or uninstall to remove the private database, including stored measurements and settings. Android app backup is disabled. Original audio files and exported reports, charts or session files are separate from private storage and remain until you delete them from their destination. Removing a session does not delete an original source file.
safety: Use low output volume. Digital level readings are not certified sound-pressure measurements. This app does not diagnose hearing or provide medical advice.
checks: Deny microphone permission and verify the app remains usable; grant it only when testing live analysis.
Start/stop analysis and background the app; confirm microphone use ends.
Select a non-sensitive audio file, inspect a spectrum, save/delete a session and export a report.
Test generation at low volume and verify Stop, route changes and privacy access.
gaps: Verify microphone denial/revocation and foreground-only operation on the final signed build.
Recheck the prepared screenshots against the final release and test native-library alignment, audio routes and exported-report accuracy on physical hardware.

name: Medical Terminology Flashcards
title: Medical Terminology Flashcards
short: Study medical word parts with flashcards, quizzes and offline practice.
description:
Build your understanding of medical terminology through focused study. Explore terms and word parts, practice with flashcards and quizzes, and assemble word parts. Favorites, spaced repetition and progress tracking help organize study sessions.

Core learning is designed to work offline. Pronunciation requires a compatible installed offline Android voice. No account is required. Designed for post-secondary and vocational learning.

This app is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any medical condition. It does not provide medical advice. Consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Published by Praxis Science Lab.
data: Study history, progress, favorites, preferences and ad frequency limits are stored in private device storage. Search text is used in memory, not stored as search history. No patient information, health records, microphone audio or location-sensor data is requested. The app has no account, application analytics, cloud synchronization or crash-reporting service. Studied terms and progress are not attached to advertising requests.
permissions: The current development release includes Google Mobile Ads Next-Gen 1.4.0 and User Messaging Platform 4.0.0, but blank production identifiers keep advertising and consent requests disabled. This policy covers that configuration. An advertising-enabled release requires an updated policy and Data safety declaration before distribution. Google ad services can process identifiers, approximate location inferred from IP, interactions and diagnostics. The package excludes the Android advertising-ID permission, which does not exclude all identifiers. Pronunciation passes selected text to an installed offline text-to-speech voice; that engine is supplied separately by its provider.
retention: Use in-app reset controls to remove the selected learning records. Settings, ad-frequency state and a storage-recovery copy can remain until all Android app storage is cleared. Clearing app storage or uninstalling removes private app records. Cloud backup and device transfer are disabled. There is no developer server copy. Device services and any future advertising providers control their own records.
safety: Educational reference only. This is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition. Consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis or treatment.
checks: Use only an approved production content build for store screenshots and release testing.
Test offline study, flashcards, quizzes, word building, progress and selective reset.
Verify offline pronunciation and behavior when no offline voice exists.
Complete TalkBack traversal and any configured consent/ad flows before release.
gaps: Production educational content is absent. Do not publish the listing as a usable released learning product or reuse synthetic test screenshots.
Final audience, health declaration, account type, advertising configuration, Data safety and manual accessibility/device checks remain open.
The existing app's embedded policy and provisional URL still require a governed update to match this public policy before distribution.

name: XLab Tools
title: XLab Tools
short: A screen ruler, digital level, tone generator and sound analysis in one app.
description:
Measure and explore with four tools on your Android phone. Calibrate the screen ruler, check tilt with the digital level, generate sine, square or triangle tones and run frequency sweeps.

Sound Meter offers live levels, an oscilloscope and an FFT spectrum. Switch views while keeping measurements and controls visible. Read the built-in Help before your first measurement; calibration and session saving have dedicated dialogs.

Save ruler and level readings, tone presets and sound-level sessions locally. Choose a light, dark or system theme and configure screen wakefulness and level haptics. The current development version works offline without an account.

Measurements depend on the phone and calibration. Sound levels are shown in dBFS until a reference adjustment is applied; adjusted SPL remains an estimate. Start generated tones at low volume. Published by Praxis Science Lab.
data: Ruler and level measurements, tone presets, sound-level statistics, session names, calibration profiles and preferences are stored on the device. Microphone samples and waveform/spectrum frames are processed temporarily in memory. They are not saved as audio files or transmitted. Saved sound sessions contain numeric level statistics and the recent level graph, not audio or analysis frames. The current version has no account, advertising, analytics or cloud service.
permissions: Microphone permission is requested when starting Sound Meter. It can be denied or revoked in Android Settings; the other tools do not need it. The level uses available motion sensors. Audio capture and tone playback stop when the app leaves the foreground. The current Android application declares no Internet permission. Advertising is planned for a future version; this notice will be updated before advertising is enabled.
retention: Clear app storage in Android Settings or uninstall to remove local measurements, calibration profiles and preferences. Android app backup is disabled in this build. Praxis Science Lab has no server copy of your measurements.
safety: Read each tool’s Help and calibrate where appropriate. Phone sensors and screen measurements have device-dependent limits. Sound Meter is not a certified sound-level meter and does not provide A-weighted dBA measurements. Use low audio output volume.
checks: Calibrate the ruler with a physical reference and check a different known length.
Set the level zero, test Hold/Resume and verify sensor use stops when leaving the tool.
At low volume, test tone waveforms, frequency changes, sweeps and Stop.
Start and stop Sound Meter, switch Level/Oscilloscope/Spectrum, read Help and save a session.
Deny microphone permission, test background behavior and check theme and saved settings after restarting.
gaps: Prepare a signed release AAB and confirm the permanent package identifier before publishing.
Validate measurements, permissions and audio behavior on representative physical devices.
Prepare final store artwork and screenshots from the release build.
Advertising is planned but not implemented. Review SDK behavior, privacy information and consent requirements before enabling it.
